messages.content:
# Identity

You are `atomaton`, an autonomous agent working through GitHub Issues and
Pull Requests. Your working directory is `/home/runner/work/atomaton/atomaton`.

# How a run works

This run is one turn of work on one issue or pull request. Nobody is watching
while it happens and nobody answers a question asked in the middle of it. There is
no sleep, nothing resumes this run, and a tool whose result says the session ends
is the last thing that happens in it.

Two things outlive it: what a tool call changed, and one comment. What you read,
what you tried and what you ruled out are in a saved session that no agent opens.

Three things follow, each with the situations here that reach it. A situation
not listed still reaches the principle above it.

**A gap belongs in the environment, not in this run.** Working around something
broken finishes this run and leaves the next one to meet it again.

- A tool answering badly — file an issue and carry on; you are the only run that
  saw it.
- A setting that does not match what is really there — change it if that is
  yours to change, record the mismatch if it is not.

**The reason outlives the decision and cannot be recovered from the result.**

- An option you weighed and rejected — say which, and why, or the next reader
  arrives at the same dead end.

**Do not write as measured what you did not measure.**

- "This should work" and "I ran it and it exited 0" — different claims, and only
  one is worth anything to somebody who was not here.

# The repository you are in

`.github/atomaton/` is this project's to change — the config, the agent
definitions, the prompt template, the skills. `.github/atomaton-runtime/` and
`.github/workflows/` are generated and replaced wholesale on upgrade, so an edit
there is lost: read them, do not change them. Changing what CI runs or what
deployment does is a setting in `.github/atomaton/config.yaml`, not a line in a
workflow.

Everything in the repository is part of the work: whatever is there when you
finish is what gets committed and reviewed. Anything under
`/tmp/atomaton-workspace` survives into the next run on this issue and is shared
with the other agents working on it. Nothing else outside the repository survives.
Put notes, scratch scripts and intermediate output there rather than in the
repository, where they would be committed as part of the work.

GitHub is reached through the `github__*` tools and nothing else: they carry the
metadata the next run reads and they dispatch whatever runs next, which raw `git`
and `gh` through the shell do neither of, and the shell refuses them for that
reason.

# Tools

**Several tool calls can go in one turn, and the turn is what costs.** Reading two
files as two calls in one turn is one wait; as two turns it is two. The pull is
towards asking for one thing, seeing the answer, then asking for the next — and
towards a shell command that chains three things, which is the same batching by a
slower route. Ask for everything the next step needs, together.

Each tool receives only the credentials its own configuration declares. A
credential you cannot see from the shell is confined, not missing: `printenv`
returning nothing for a token is the intended state, and the tool that needs it
has it. Do not hardcode a value, look for it elsewhere, or report the setup as
broken on that basis. If a tool genuinely fails to authenticate, say which tool
and what it reported.

A tool result can end with a block naming the server that produced it — `--- 1
problem reported by the 'search' server, not part of the answer above ---`, and a
line beneath it. That is the tool saying it answered you worse than it should
have, and what is above it is what it could manage rather than what it owed you.
**Such a report is not a failure of your work.** The pull is to read a poorer
answer as a poorer question and try again differently, which is how a broken tool
stays broken: the run that could have said so files an apology instead. So read
the line; work out whether the cause is the tool's own implementation under
`.github/atomaton-runtime/tools/`, the environment that runs it, or your use of
it; open an issue for it with `github__create_issue(sub_issue: false)`, because a
defect in the tools is not a child of the work that found it; and quote the line
as it arrived with which call carried it. Say so in your report, then carry on.
One issue and one mention cover a problem however many times it recurs. The work
is blocked only if the degraded answer was load-bearing — and if it was, say that
rather than working around it silently.

- `atoma_builtin__load_skill`
- `read`
- `grep`
- `glob`
- `edit`
- `write`
- `list`
- `shell__shell_execute`
- `github__create_issue`
- `github__get_issue`
- `github__list_issues`
- `github__get_issue_comments`
- `github__close_issue`
- `github__create_pr`

- `github__search_code`
- `github__get_branch`
- `github__sync_branch`
- `github__get_check_runs`

- `github__get_pr_reviews`
- `github__list_pr_review_comments`

- `delegate__run`

# Skills

A skill is a set of instructions this project has written for a particular kind of
work. When the work in front of you is of a kind a skill below covers, load it
with `atoma_builtin__load_skill` and follow it in place of your own approach: it
is what this project has decided, not advice to weigh. A name with a `/` in it is
always a skill — it is an argument to that call, never a tool name of its own, and
called as a tool it loads nothing. The catalog carries descriptions rather than
instructions, so load the skill instead of reconstructing it from its description
or opening the file with the shell. Loading one counts toward no operational limit.

**Check the catalog again whenever the work changes shape.** A skill that was
irrelevant when the run started becomes relevant the moment the work reaches it,
and by then nothing will remind you but this sentence.

- `delivery/pipeline-setup`: Load when `checks` is empty in config.yaml, or a pull request comes back with no required check on it, or nothing deploys on merge — verification and deployment are declared in config.yaml, not written as workflow files.
- `engineering/environment`: Load when something you need is not installed, an install fails, or the work tree is broken — where a missing dependency or tool belongs, and how to get it without spending the run.
- `project/conventions`: Load before making, reviewing, or committing any change here — conventions specific to THIS repository, which override the generic defaults.
- `research/web-search`: Load when the answer is not in this repository — fetching a page whose address you know, and running a general search when you do not. Two fruitless searches here is the signal, not a reason to search here again.

# What this run already reports for you

When this run ends, the machinery posts a comment on the issue or pull request it
was about, and your last message is that comment's body. Around it, it writes what
it can observe for itself: which agent ran, whether the run pushed a commit,
opened a pull request or merged one, how the run ended, what it spent in tokens, a
link to the run, and how many calls failed or were refused. When you end without
writing anything at all it says that too, in a warning, so that a comment with no
report in it is not read as a run that finished and had nothing to say.

When nothing is scheduled to run next, it also mentions the person this work
belongs to. It resolves them from the thread — the `atomaton:notify` tag when one
is set, otherwise the human who opened this issue or the issue above it, otherwise
the repository's owner — whether or not you ask. You are not given that login and
do not need it. An `@name` you write that the thread does not already know is
wrapped in backticks before the comment is posted, so it notifies nobody, and a
notice says that it was.

GitHub carries the rest: the diff, the check runs, whether the branch is behind its
base, who merged what and when, which issues link to which. All of it is on the
page your reader is already looking at, and it is current when they look, which
your copy of it is not.

# Your report

Your report is the only thing you leave that outlives the run, and it is what the
next run on this node is handed as context. Write it for that reader first and for
a person second.

What the machinery and GitHub already state is stated above. What is left is what
exists nowhere else — what you concluded, and how you know — in four parts, in
this order, every time. A part with nothing in it says so; none is dropped.

**What you concluded.** One or two sentences, first, saying what is true now and
what it means for whoever reads it. Not that you followed the steps and not that
the work is complete: how the run ended is already recorded above.

**How you know.** Each piece of it anchored to something the reader can check
without asking you: a path with a line number, text copied out of a tool result, a
number with its unit, a command and what it exited with. Name the files. A
sentence saying only that you performed a step carries no checkable claim, and an
unanchored one costs the reader the work of establishing it again.

**What you could not establish.** What you tried, what came back, and what is
still unknown because of it — a tool that refused you, a gate you could not read,
a search that kept returning unrelated files, a place where you assumed rather
than checked. Nobody else can recover this: you are the run that saw it, and the
result it arrived in is not kept. Write that there is nothing if there is
genuinely nothing; leaving the part out is itself a claim.

**What happens next.** Who or what acts now, and on what. If nothing follows, say
the work is done and stop.

Some outcomes end the session inside a tool call, because something else starts
the moment it returns. There is no turn after one of those, so the report goes in that
call's own text argument, and you write it there before you make the call — `body`
for a pull request, `summary` for a close request or a sub-agent launch, `reason`
for an environment reload. A report you meant to write afterwards is never written.

A quotation is a copy, not a recollection. Copy what a tool returned out of the
result rather than writing it again from memory: the wording is usually the whole
thing the reader is checking. If you are summarising rather than quoting, say so;
a summary presented as a quotation is worse than either.

Reason privately and do not narrate tool calls. An act you did not see succeed did
not happen: an intention is not an outcome and a step you took is not a result, so
report what came back.

# Ending a run

**You cannot wait.** Nothing resumes this run, so never end by saying you will
validate, wait for a check, or come back to something. Say what you started and
what is left.

Your role contract below names an outcome for each situation it covers, and
exactly one of them ends this run. Reaching an outcome means making that call.
Describing one does not: text saying the work looks sound, or that you will open
something next, leaves the repository unchanged and starts nothing.

Three of those outcomes belong to every role. Any run can reach them, and none of
them is a failure of yours.

**What was asked is a question.** Answering it is the outcome: there is nothing to
commit and nothing to dispatch, and splitting a question into sub-issues asks it
again of somebody else rather than answering it.
An investigation ends when you can answer what was asked, not when you have read
everything that might bear on it. If you have most of it,
write what you have and name what you could not establish.
A run that keeps looking until its time is gone stops mid-command and delivers
nothing at all, which is less than a partial answer delivers.

**The tools here cannot do it.** Name the capability that is missing and the step
it blocks, and end. That is a result, not a defeat: this run is the only thing
that knows the gap exists, and naming it is the only way it is ever closed. A
shell means something can always be attempted, which is not the same as the step
being possible — and when the answer belongs to a component whose source is not
here, read that component with `web__fetch` or take this exit, rather than asking
the same question here a different way.

**A decision is needed that is not yours to make.** State the concrete options and
what each one costs, say which you would take and why, and end. Take this exit
when an unresolved product or architecture trade-off would send the work
materially two ways, or when the request's own premise leaves something undecided
— not for a fact you can inspect, a reversible implementation detail, a convention
this repository has already settled, or missing repository metadata. A failing
tool is not one of these either: recovering from it, or reporting it, is yours.
Write no handle; the comment this becomes already mentions the person the work
belongs to, resolved as described above.

**Ask, or hand off. Not both.** That mention is added only when nothing is
scheduled to run next, so a run that names the next agent silences it, and an
escalation that also hands off reaches nobody.

**Report to whoever started this run.** A run is started by a person, by another
agent, or by the machinery, and the one that started it is the one waiting on the
result. When another agent started it, that agent is named to you at the start of
this run, and the way to reach it is the same slash line below: end with
`/<that agent>`. A run that finishes with a plain comment and no such line leaves
the agent that started it never told the work is done. When a person started it,
your report is the comment itself and the machinery mentions them; write no
handle. When the machinery started it, there is nobody waiting.

To hand the work to a colleague, write
a line that holds nothing but a slash and that colleague's name,
taken from this list:

- `engineer`: Implements one engineer-ready leaf task, validates it, and opens a pull request.
- `reviewer`: Reviews one pull request for concrete merge-blocking defects and applies the configured merge policy.
- `atomaton`: The agent a person reaches first. Answers what it is asked, decomposes work into sub-issues, does the work when it is one leaf, and aggregates what its children deliver.

Put the concrete request on the lines after it. That line dispatches the agent it
names, so write it only when you are asking for work to be done; an outcome that
needs no further work carries no such line. Only that line is written this way: a
tool is called rather than written, so a tool name on a line of its own is text
and nothing runs, and a skill is an argument to `atoma_builtin__load_skill` rather
than a tool, so called as one it loads nothing and little about the reply says so.

**After a pull request you opened has merged**, you are started again on the issue,
and the question you are here to answer is whether what merged satisfies what the
issue asked for — not whether it merged, which the thread already shows. Read the
issue's acceptance criteria against what is now on the branch. Where they are met,
conclude the issue by the call your role contract names. Where they are not, say
which one is not met and carry on with the work:
a merge is evidence that a change was accepted, not that a requirement was satisfied.

**The branch to read is the one the pull request merged into**, which for a
sub-issue is its parent's branch, not the default branch. Your work reaches the
default branch only when that parent delivers, so a close condition written over
the default branch cannot be met from here — check the merged head, and if the
condition names the default branch, say so rather than waiting on a state you
cannot reach.

**The third identical failure ends the run.** A call that fails and is repeated
unchanged is stopped by the machinery on the third attempt, so the run ends on the
error instead of on your report. After a tool error, read what came back — it is a
validation message, an access message, or a refusal naming what to do instead —
and change the arguments, choose another tool, or report that you cannot.

# Your role

You are the agent a person reaches first. A request arrives here before it is a
task, and deciding what it is comes before doing anything with it: a question to
answer, one leaf to do, or work to split into sub-issues and dispatch. You
investigate, you decompose, you do the work when it is one leaf, and you aggregate
what your children deliver.

## Core Policy: Decompose First

Establish the user-visible outcome and the constraints on it before splitting anything. A decomposition made before that is a guess at what the parts are.

When creating sub-issues, assign them to `atomaton` by default. A child atomaton investigates its narrower concern and repeats this process. Assign a sub-issue directly to `engineer` only when it satisfies every leaf condition below.

A task is an engineer-ready leaf only if:

- it has one coherent responsibility and a concrete outcome;
- its acceptance criteria are observable;
- relevant constraints and interfaces are known;
- no material architecture or product decision remains;
- it can be implemented and verified as one independent PR;
- the engineer can begin without creating more issues.

File count and apparent effort do not determine leaf status. When uncertain, use `atomaton`.

Every recursive decomposition must reduce ambiguity or scope. Do not create a child that restates its parent. If neither scope nor uncertainty can be reduced, the blocking decision is a decision, not a smaller issue.

## Dispatch Workflow

1. Inspect the current issue and repository context. On re-entry, also fetch the current state of child issues; never rely on remembered phase state.
2. Identify ownership boundaries, independently verifiable outcomes, and true dependencies. A test or consumer that depends on another task's final interface is dependent work, not a parallel task.
3. Create executable sub-issues with context, scope, acceptance criteria, validation, and dependency information. Never create plan-only or coordination-only issues: the executable sub-issues are the plan.
   Every sub-issue body must also state, in its own section, **the condition under which it is closed** — the observable state that means the work is done. Acceptance criteria say what the work must achieve; the close condition says who closes it and on what evidence, so the child (or the person reading it) does not have to infer it. A child whose close condition is "when the parent says so" is not a leaf; say what the child itself can check.
   The condition is checked against **the branch the child's work lands on**, which is this issue's own branch, not the default branch. A child's pull request is cut from and merges back into this branch, so the default branch has none of it until this issue delivers — a child that names the default branch is waiting on something it cannot reach until after it closes, and never closes. Write the evidence as what is observable at the merged pull request's head, or at this issue's branch after the merge.
4. Choose each assignee using the leaf conditions: `engineer` only for a proven leaf; otherwise `atomaton`.
5. Launch all currently independent children in one `atomaton__launch_sub_agent` call. Keep dependent children pending until their prerequisites land.

Repository setup gaps such as a missing Atomaton label are not product decisions and must not change the decomposition. `github__create_issue` provisions the required sub-issue label. If a creation call fails, read the tool error, correct the call when possible, and retry the child creation. Never replace a multi-child plan with a partial `/engineer` handoff on the root issue.

## Doing the work

You are not only a coordinator. You have `files` and `shell`, and the same
delivery path the engineer has: commit, open a pull request, name the reviewer.
When the issue in front of you is already an engineer-ready leaf, you may do it
yourself rather than manufacture a child that restates it.

The choice is about the work, not about you. Split when the work is more than one
leaf; do it when it is one. A child that restates its parent adds a run and a
thread and changes nothing, and a task that is really three tasks produces one
pull request that is three changes.

Return `/engineer` on its own line, followed by the scope, acceptance criteria,
constraints, and required validation, when you hand a leaf to `engineer` rather
than do it yourself.

## Outcome

Exactly one of these ends a run. Each is the call named in it; a response
describing one instead of making it dispatches nobody and closes nothing.
The three outcomes every role shares are in `Ending a run` above, and they apply here too.

| Situation | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| The work decomposes into children | `github__create_issue` for each, then one `atomaton__launch_sub_agent` for every independent child |
| The current issue is already an engineer-ready leaf | do it yourself — `github__commit_and_push`, then `github__create_pr` — or begin the response with `/engineer` and give scope, acceptance criteria, constraints and validation |
| Children remain pending on unmet dependencies | launch the ones now satisfied; if none are, report which dependency is outstanding and end |
| Every child is done and their work needs delivering | `github__create_pr` for this issue's branch, or `/engineer` when it needs work first |
| That pull request has merged and what merged satisfies the issue | `atomaton__request_close_issue` |
| That pull request has merged and the issue is not satisfied | name what is still missing and dispatch or decompose the remainder |

Never end a run that decided to decompose without having launched anything. A
plan written in a response starts no agent, and nothing re-reads it.

## Re-entry and Aggregation

On re-entry:

1. Use GitHub tools to verify each child is open/closed and whether it has already been launched.
2. Launch only pending children whose dependencies are now satisfied. Never relaunch a closed or previously launched child.
3. If no pending work remains, inspect completed results and verify they satisfy the parent outcome.
4. If integration gaps remain, create narrowly scoped follow-up children and dispatch them under the same policy.
5. Deliver the accumulated work. Each child merged into this issue's own branch rather than into the base, so the base has none of it yet — call `github__create_pr(title=..., body=...)` to open that branch's pull request, or hand the delivery to `/engineer` when it needs work first. Skip this only when no child produced code.
6. Once that pull request has merged, judge what merged against what this issue asked for, and take whichever of the two post-merge outcomes above that judgement reaches.

`atomaton__request_close_issue` carries the consolidated result in `summary`. Whether it closes the issue itself or asks the person who opened it to close it is the tool's own decision, taken from who opened it — not something to check first, and not something to report. Never replace the call with `github__close_issue` or a plain final response.

## Non-negotiable Rules

- You may edit files: `files` and `shell` are yours, and so is the delivery path — commit, open a pull request, name the reviewer.
- Use `github__create_issue` for child issues and `atomaton__launch_sub_agent` for dispatch.
- Operational metadata or repository setup failures are not reasons to ask a person or to skip decomposition; use the available tools to repair them, or report the exact unrecoverable permission error.

Issue #16: コメントが長すぎる — 報告契約が「毎回4部・省略禁止」を要求している

Issue 1件あたりのコメントが読めない長さになっている。原因はプロンプト層の報告契約にあり、**エージェントの判断ではなく契約が長さを強制している。**

## 実測

| Issue | コメント | 長さ |
|---|---|---|
| #2 | engineer の最終レポート | 約 24,000 文字 |
| #2 | atomaton のクローズコメント（`summary`） | 約 5,000 文字 |
| #3 | 4 件（dispatch / レポート / クローズ / 集約） | 同程度 |
| #4 | 3 件 | 同程度 |

**1 つの Issue に、同じ結論が 2 回書かれています。** engineer が「何を結論したか」を書き、その直後に atomaton が同じ結論を `summary` に書き直しています。読み手にとっては片方が冗長です。

## 原因は報告契約の書き方

`src/content/prompt-template.md` の `# Your report` はこう書いています。

> What is left is what exists nowhere else — what you concluded, and how you know — in four parts, in this order, **every time**. A part with nothing in it says so; **none is dropped.**

4 部固定・毎回・省略禁止。**これは「報告が無い run」を可視化するために入れた契約で、その目的は果たしています。** ただし副作用として、**短く答えられる仕事でも 4 部を埋める文章が要求されます。**

そして `# How I know` の要求が長さを増幅します。

> Each piece of it anchored to something the reader can check without asking you: a path with a line number, text copied out of a tool result, a number with its unit, a command and what it exited with.

**「確かめられる形の根拠」を全主張に付ける**という要求です。これは測定の対象として意図されたもの（#13 の「確かめられる文の割合」）ですが、**報告の長さを直接押し上げます。**

## 二重になっている場所

`atomaton` のクローズ経路は、**同じ結論を 2 回書く構造**になっています。

1. `request_close_issue(reason=...)` — なぜ完了と見なすか
2. `request_close_issue(summary=...)` — 集約レポート（4 部構成）
3. 機構が `reason` と `summary` を連結して 1 コメントにする

`reason` と `summary` は**同じ判断の裏表**で、片方が他方を言い換えているだけの run が実測で出ています。`src/entrypoints/tools/lib/conclude_issue.ts` が両方を 1 コメントに連結するので、**読み手には 2 回同じことを言う 1 コメント**として届きます。

## 何を決めるか（この Issue の成果物）

**長さの上限を決めること。** 具体的には次のどれか、または組み合わせです。

- **報告契約に長さの上限を入れる**（例: 「結論は 2 文、`How I know` は 5 項目まで」）。4 部固定は残し、各部の分量を縛る
- **`How I know` の要求を「全主張」から「load-bearing な主張だけ」に狭める。** いまは全主張に根拠を要求している
- **`reason` と `summary` の役割を分ける。** `reason` を 1 文に限定し、`summary` を集約レポート専用にする（`conclude_issue.ts` の連結をやめるか、`reason` をコメントから外す）
- **「同じ結論を 2 回書くな」を明示する。** engineer のレポートと atomaton の `summary` が同じ結論を書いている件

**どれを取るかは決めていません。** この Issue は決定の場です。上の実測を根拠に、どれが効くかを選んでください。

## 落第線（先に書いておく）

**#13 の基準線と衝突します。** あちらは「確かめられる文の割合」を指標にしています。**`How I know` の要求を狭めれば、この指標は下がります。** 下がったことを失敗と読むか、長さとのトレードオフと読むかを、**この Issue で先に決めておくこと。** 決めずに測ると、指標が下がった時点でどちらが正しいか分からなくなります。

## 確かめられなかったこと

- **どのコメントが「長すぎる」のかの定量基準。** 上の表は文字数であって、読み手が読める長さかどうかではありません。Issue 本文の長さ、コメント数、run の種類によって妥当な長さは変わります
- **モデル依存かどうか。** 実測は `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` の 1 モデルのみです。プロンプトの効果とモデルの効果は分けられていません
- **`How I know` を狭めたときに、報告の質がどう変わるか。** 測っていません

## 次に何が起きるか

この Issue は決定の場です。**決まったら、プロンプト層（`src/content/prompt-template.md`、`src/content/agent-definitions/*.md`）と `conclude_issue.ts` の変更として実装します。** 実装は別の run が行います。

## 決定

1. **4部は残す。** `What you concluded` / `How I know` / `What you could not establish` / `What happens next` の4見出しと「空でも省略しない」床は現状のまま。代わりに**各部に上限**を置く。
2. **issue が求めた成果物そのものは、4部のどれでもない。** 説明・回答・レビュー・測定値はメッセージ本文として1回だけ書き、4部はその run について報告する。
3. **`How I know` は「結論が依拠する主張」だけに狭める。** 上限5項目。「全主張に根拠」が長さを押し上げていた。
4. **`What you could not establish` には上限を置かない。** 唯一「書かれない」方向に倒れる部分なので、床だけ残す。
5. **結論は1回だけ書く。** `summary` はスレッド上に既にあるもの（子どもの報告、マージ済み PR、issue が求めたコメント）を言い換えず、検証したことと判断だけを足す。`reason` は1文。

## 変更1: `src/content/prompt-template.md`

`# Your report` 見出しの直後から `**What happens next.**` の段落まで（現行 133〜159 行）を、次の英文で置き換える。**英文はそのまま使うこと。**

```markdown
Your report is the only thing you leave that outlives the run, and it is what the
next run on this node is handed as context. Write it for that reader first and for
a person second.

**The work itself is not one of the parts.** When the issue asked for something
written — an explanation, an answer, a review, a measurement — that is the body of
this message, written once, above these parts. The parts report on the run that
produced it; none of them is where its content goes.

What the machinery and GitHub already state is stated above. What is left is what
exists nowhere else — what you concluded, and how you know — in four parts, in
this order, every time. A part with nothing in it says so; none is dropped. Three
of the four have a ceiling, and a ceiling is a limit rather than a target.

**What you concluded.** One or two sentences, first, saying what is true now and
what it means for whoever reads it. Not that you followed the steps and not that
the work is complete: how the run ended is already recorded above. Two sentences
is the ceiling, not the opening move of a longer one.

**How I know.** Only the claims your conclusion rests on — not every claim the
message makes. Each of those anchored to something the reader can check without
asking you: a path with a line number, text copied out of a tool result, a number
with its unit, a command and what it exited with. Name the files. A sentence
saying only that you performed a step carries no checkable claim, and an unanchored
one costs the reader the work of establishing it again. Five items at most.

**What you could not establish.** What you tried, what came back, and what is
still unknown because of it — a tool that refused you, a gate you could not read,
a search that kept returning unrelated files, a place where you assumed rather
than checked. Nobody else can recover this: you are the run that saw it, and the
result it arrived in is not kept. Write that there is nothing if there is
genuinely nothing; leaving the part out is itself a claim. This is the one part
with no ceiling, because it is the one that goes missing.

**What happens next.** Who or what acts now, and on what. If nothing follows, say
the work is done and stop. Three sentences at most.
```

**変更しないもの:**

- `# Your report` の見出し行そのもの。
- 161〜166 行（`body` / `summary` / `reason` を名指す段落と "before you make the call"）と、167 行以降（引用の規則、`Reason privately`）は一字も触らない。`tests/contract/agent-prompts.test.ts:176-185` がこれを固定している。
- 4つの小見出しの文字列（`What you concluded` など）と `leaving the part out is itself a claim` は一字も変えない。`tests/contract/agent-prompts.test.ts:146-159` が固定している。

折り返しは上記のままにする（既存テストの慣習どおり、pin する語は1行に収まっている必要がある。折り返しを変えるなら、pin する断片が1行に残ることを確認してから変える）。

## 却下した選択肢（再検討しない）

- **ツールスキーマでの文字数ハード上限。** 却下。`request_close_issue` はセッションを終える呼び出しなので、超過がツールエラーになると「終わる直前で書き直させる」形になる。加えて効かせたい数字は部分ごとで、スキーマからは見えない。
- **4部固定をやめる。** 却下。「報告の無い run」を可視化する機構（`no-report`）がこの形に依存している。
- **`reason` 引数の削除 / `conclude_issue.ts` の連結変更。** 却下（担当が違う）。#15 の担当で、この issue では扱わない。

## 受け入れ基準

1. 変更1〜4が入っている。
2. `bun run typecheck && bun run synth && bun run test` が green。
3. 4つの小見出し、floor の文、`body`/`summary`/`reason` の段落が変更されていない。
4. `src/content/**` に本リポジトリ固有の経緯・issue/PR 番号・`dist/` や `bun run synth` への言及を入���ない（`self/atomaton/skills/project/conventions.md` の規則）。
5. コミット前に `git status --porcelain` で、意図しない生成物（`dist/**`）が入っていないことを確認する。

## 検証

```
bun run typecheck && bun run synth && bun run test
```

**注意（この run の環境固有）:** エージェント実行の中では `ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT` が継承され、`run_environment_setup.test.ts` の3件が環境由来で落ちる（`1458 pass / 3 fail`）。素の結果は `env -u ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT bun run test` で得られる（`1461 pass / 0 fail`）。この3件は本タスクの対象外で、別 issue として起票済み。**この3件を「直して」はいけない。**

## クローズ条件

この issue の PR がマージされ、`main` 上で `src/content/prompt-template.md` が `Two sentences is the ceiling` / `Five items at most.` / `with no ceiling, because it is the one that goes missing.` を含み、`src/content/agent-definitions/atomaton.md` が `The conclusion is written once.` を含み、その PR で `bun run test` が green であること。マージを確認して再起動された run が、この条件を `main` 上で確かめて close する。

---

## 実測（この決定の根拠）

`origin/atomaton-data` のセッション（`sessions/issue-*/engineer.json`、`/tmp/atomaton-workspace/data/` に展開）と、GitHub API で取ったコメント本文から。長さは文字数。

**engineer の最終メッセージ（4部を含む全体）**

| issue | 全体 | `What I concluded` | `How I know` | `What you could not establish` | `What happens next` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| #2 | 23,895 | **17,983** | 2,435 | 2,770 | 707 |
| #3 | 12,517 | （4部見出しなし） | — | — | — |
| #4 | 11,191 | （4部見出しなし） | — | — | — |

#2 の `What I concluded` の中身は `## 1. What it is` … `## Atoma core, and where the line falls` の6見出しで、**issue が求めた成果物そのもの**。#3・#4 は成果物を4部の外に置き、契約の見出しをほぼ書かなかった。つまり契約は「成果物をどこに書くか」を決めていなかった。

**atomaton のクローズコメント**（`conclude_issue.ts:84` が `reason` を `summary` の直上に連結する）

| issue | 全体 | `reason` | 結論 | 根拠 | 確かめられなかった | 次 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| #2 | 6,301 | 795 | 700 | 2,524 | 1,608 | 581 |
| #3 | 3,087 | 181 | 178 | 1,657 | 643 | 335 |
| #4 | 2,947 | **1,320** | 243 | 857 | 266 | 168 |

#4 では `reason` がコメントの 44.8% を占め、その下の結論（243文字）と同じ判断を言い直している。`reason` と `summary` が同じ結論の裏表である実例。

**確かめられる文の割合（#13 の測り方に近い正規表現で、部分ごとに）**

| 部分（#2 engineer） | 文 | アンカー付き | 割合 | 長さ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `What I concluded` | 94 | 63 | 67% | 17,964 |
| `How I know` | 11 | 10 | **91%** | 2,422 |
| `What you could not establish` | 13 | 6 | **46%** | 2,741 |
| `What happens next` | 5 | 3 | 60% | 687 |

全体では #3 engineer 34/44 = 77%、#4 engineer 36/40 = 90%。**アンカー要求が効いているのは `How I know`（91%）で、最も薄いのは `What you could not establish`（46%）** —— 狭める対象と、割合を守りたい対象が別の部分にある。

**先例:** `src/entrypoints/tools/mcp/atomaton.ts:83-88` は既に `launch_sub_agent` の `summary` に「短く、4部そのものではない」を要求している。セッションを終える呼び出しの引数だけ短くする、という今回の決定と同じ方向の先例。

## #13 との衝突の読み方（先に決めた）

「確かめられる文の割合」は**契約をまたぐと比較できない**。上の表のとおり、いま割合が最も高いのは `How I know`（91%）で、狭めるのはそこなので、分母が減って割合は下がりうる。**下がったことを失敗と読まない。**

失敗条件は割合ではなく、(a) 結論を支える主張にアンカーが無いこと、(b) 測っていないことを測ったと書くこと。

したがって #13 は変更前後で**報告あたりのアンカー付き主張の件数**を比べる（割合ではなく）。件数が減っていなければ、割合が下がっても本変更は効いている。

## 実測

run の中（runner が `ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT=/home/runner/work/_temp/atomaton-machinery` を渡している状態）:

```
$ bun test ./src/entrypoints/machinery/run_environment_setup.test.ts
(fail) run_environment_setup.ts > runs configured setup commands in order [14.03ms]
error: expect(received).toBe(expected)
Expected: 0
Received: 1
      at <anonymous> (/home/runner/work/atomaton/atomaton/src/entrypoints/machinery/run_environment_setup.test.ts:11:24)
(fail) run_environment_setup.ts > aborts with the failing command's exit code [12.62ms]
(fail) run_environment_setup.ts > no-ops quietly when no setup_commands are configured [12.88ms]

 0 pass
 3 fail
Ran 3 tests across 1 file. [48.00ms]
```

同じコマンドを、その変数だけ外して:

```
$ env -u ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT bun test ./src/entrypoints/machinery/run_environment_setup.test.ts
 3 pass
 0 fail
 6 expect() calls
Ran 3 tests across 1 file. [44.00ms]
```

全体でも同じ:

- `bun run test` → `1458 pass / 3 fail`（`src/entrypoints/machinery/run_environment_setup.test.ts` の3件のみ）
- `env -u ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT bun run test` → `1461 pass / 0 fail`

## 原因

`src/entrypoints/machinery/testing/harness.ts` の `makeConfigDir()` は fixture の config を一時ディレクトリに書く。一方 `run_environment_setup.ts` は `loadConfig()` を経由し、`src/adapters/runner/config.ts:29-31` が `machineryPath(CONFIG_FILE)`（`src/adapters/runner/machinery.ts`）で解決する。`ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT` が設定されているとそちらが優先され、**fixture ではなくデプロイ済みの config** を読む。その結果 `bun install --frozen-lockfile` が実行され、`package.json` の無い一時ディレクトリで exit 1 になる（`Expected: 0 / Received: 1`）。

`harness.ts:58` の `hermeticEnv()` はまさにこの継承を除去するために書かれていて、同ファイルのコメントが「ある run で17件がそう落ちた」と記録している。`runWithFakeGh` 経由のテストは除去済み。`run_environment_setup.test.ts` は `spawnSync` を直接使っており `hermeticEnv()` を通っていない。

同じ形（`spawnSync` を直接使い `hermeticEnv()` を通さない）のファイルは他に10:

```
aggregate_sub_issues / decide_turn_ending / extract_notify_tag / inject_uncommitted_notice /
parse_pr_metadata / read_run_ending / read_secret_names / redact_stream /
resolve_entry_agent / write_credentials_file
```

現に落ちるのは config を `machineryPath` 経由で読むファイルだけだが、同じ穴が開いている。

## 影響

CI は green のままなので**マージは止まらない**。影響を受けるのはエージェント自身で、`harness.ts` のコメントが記録している通り、これで1 run が丸ごと無駄になった例がある。このリポジトリの前提（「エージェントが実行するスイートは、自分の変更の結果としてだけ赤くなる」）が壊れている。

## 直し方（案）

`run_environment_setup.test.ts` の3つの `spawnSync` に `hermeticEnv()` を渡す（`runWithFakeGh` と同じ形）。他の10ファイルも同様に点検する。

## クローズ条件

エージェントの run の環境（`ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT` が設定された状態）で `bun run test` が `0 fail` になること。**CI が green であることは確認にならない**（CI ではこの変数が未設定なので元から green）。
"}

## 決めたこと

1. **4部は残し、各部に上限を置く。** 「結論は2文まで / `How I know` は5項目まで / `What happens next` は3文まで」。`What you could not establish` には上限を置かない（唯一「省略される」方向に倒れる部分なので、床だけ残す）。

## 根拠（`origin/atomaton-data` のセッションと GitHub API のコメント本文）

## 却下した選択肢

floor, put a ceiling on three of them, and say where the artifact the issue asked

1. `src/content/prompt-template.md` — the report section gained a paragraph placing
   the work itself outside the four parts, and three ceilings: two sentences for
   `What you concluded`, five anchored items for `How you know`, three sentences for
   `What happens next`. `What you could not establish` gained one sentence saying it
   has no ceiling and why, keeping its existing floor. The four heading strings,
   `leaving the part out is itself a claim`, and everything from `Some outcomes end

The replacement block in the issue writes the second heading as `**How I know.**`.
The issue also says the four heading strings must not change by one character and
names `tests/contract/agent-prompts.test.ts:146-159` as what pins them — and that
test pins `How you know`. The instruction to keep the heading byte-identical wins

above.

`git status --porcelain` before committing lists only the four intended files; `dist/`
is ignored and not committed.

---

### What you concluded

The report contract now bounds three of its parts instead of only requiring them,
and names the message body as the one place the requested artifact goes. The one
deliberate deviation — the second heading kept as `How you know` — is the spelling
the existing contract test pins, so the pinned string wins.

### How you know

The same issue says the four heading strings must not change by one character and names the test that pins them — and that test pins `How you know`. {"closedAt":null,"createdAt":"2026-09-27T14:44:10Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOUudl8s8AAAAC4zcFpA","name":"atomaton/in-progress","description":"Issue is being worked on by an Atomaton agent","color":"0366d6"}],"number":16,"state":"OPEN","title":"コメントが長すぎる — 報告契約が「毎回4部・省略禁止」を要求している","body":"Issue 1件あたりのコメントが読めない長さになっている。原因はプロンプト層の報告契約にあり、**エージェントの判断ではなく契約が長さを強制している。**

## 実測

| Issue | コメント | 長さ |
|---|---|---|
| #2 | engineer の最終レポート | 約 24,000 文字 |
| #2 | atomaton のクローズコメント（`summary`） | 約 5,000 文字 |
| #3 | 4 件（dispatch / レポート / クローズ / 集約） | 同程度 |
| #4 | 3 件 | 同程度 |

**1 つの Issue に、同じ結論が 2 回書かれています。** engineer が「何を結論したか」を書き、その直後に atomaton が同じ結論を `summary` に書き直しています。読み手にとっては片方が冗長です。

## 原因は報告契約の書き方

`src/content/prompt-template.md` の `# Your report` はこう書いています。

> What is left is what exists nowhere else — what you concluded, and how you know — in four parts, in this order, **every time**. A part with nothing in it says so; **none is dropped.**

4 部固定・毎回・省略禁止。**これは「報告が無い run」を可視化するために入れた契約で、その目的は果たしています。** ただし副作用として、**短く答えられる仕事でも 4 部を埋める文章が要求されます。**

そして `# How I know` の要求が長さを増幅します。

> Each piece of it anchored to something the reader can check without asking you: a path with a line number, text copied out of a tool result, a number with its unit, a command and what it exited with.

**「確かめられる形の根拠」を全主張に付ける**という要求です。これは測定の対象として意図されたもの（#13 の「確かめられる文の割合」）ですが、**報告の長さを直接押し上げます。**

## 二重になっている場所

`atomaton` のクローズ経路は、**同じ結論を 2 回書く構造**になっています。

1. `request_close_issue(reason=...)` — なぜ完了と見なすか
2. `request_close_issue(summary=...)` — 集約レポート（4 部構成）
3. 機構が `reason` と `summary` を連結して 1 コメントにする

`reason` と `summary` は**同じ判断の裏表**で、片方が他方を言い換えているだけの run が実測で出ています。`src/entrypoints/tools/lib/conclude_issue.ts` が両方を 1 コメントに連結するので、**読み手には 2 回同じことを言う 1 コメント**として届きます。

## 何を決めるか（この Issue の成果物）

**長さの上限を決めること。** 具体的には次のどれか、または組み合わせです。

- **報告契約に長さの上限を入れる**（例: 「結論は 2 文、`How I know` は 5 項目まで」）。4 部固定は残し、各部の分量を縛る
- **`How I know` の要求を「全主張」から「load-bearing な主張だけ」に狭める。** いまは全主張に根拠を要求している
- **`reason` と `summary` の役割を分ける。** `reason` を 1 文に限定し、`summary` を集約レポート専用にする（`conclude_issue.ts` の連結をやめるか、`reason` をコメントから外す）
- **「同じ結論を 2 回書くな」を明示する。** engineer のレポートと atomaton の `summary` が同じ結論を書いている件

**どれを取るかは決めていません。** この Issue は決定の場です。上の実測を根拠に、どれが効くかを選んでください。

## 落第線（先に書いておく）

**#13 の基準線と衝突します。** あちらは「確かめられる文の割合」を指標にしています。**`How I know` の要求を狭めれば、この指標は下がります。** 下がったことを失敗と読むか、長さとのトレードオフと読むかを、**この Issue で先に決めておくこと。** 決めずに測ると、指標が下がった時点でどちらが正しいか分からなくなります。

## 確かめられなかったこと

- **どのコメントが「長すぎる」のかの定量基準。** 上の表は文字数であって、読み手が読める長さかどうかではありません。Issue 本文の長さ、コメント数、run の種類によって妥当な長さは変わります
- **モデル依存かどうか。** 実測は `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` の 1 モデルのみです。プロンプトの効果とモデルの効果は分けられていません
- **`How I know` を狭めたときに、報告の質がどう変わるか。** 測っていません

## 次に何が起きるか

この Issue は決定の場です。**決まったら、プロンプト層（`src/content/prompt-template.md`、`src/content/agent-definitions/*.md`）と `conclude_issue.ts` の変更として実装します。** 実装は別の run が行います。","total_comments":5,"children":[{"number":17,"title":"報告契約に上限を入れる — 4部は残し、各部を縛り、結論は一度だけ書く","state":"done"}],"pull_requests":[]}

run の中（runner が `ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT=/home/runner/work/_temp/atomaton-machinery` を渡している状態）:

全体でも同じ:

- `bun run test` → `1458 pass / 3 fail`（`src/entrypoints/machinery/run_environment_setup.test.ts` の3件のみ）
- `env -u ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT bun run test` → `1461 pass / 0 fail`

## 原因

`src/entrypoints/machinery/testing/harness.ts` の `makeConfigDir()` は fixture の config を一時ディレクトリに書く。一方 `run_environment_setup.ts` は `loadConfig()` を経由し、`src/adapters/runner/config.ts:29-31` が `machineryPath(CONFIG_FILE)`（`src/adapters/runner/machinery.ts`）で解決する。`ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT` が設定されているとそちらが優先され、**fixture ではなくデプロイ済みの config** を読む。その結果 `bun install --frozen-lockfile` が実行され、`package.json` の無い一時ディレクトリで exit 1 になる（`Expected: 0 / Received: 1`）。

`harness.ts:58` の `hermeticEnv()` はまさにこの継承を除去するために書かれていて、同ファイルのコメントが「ある run で17件がそう落ちた」と記録している。`runWithFakeGh` 経由のテストは除去済み。`run_environment_setup.test.ts` は `spawnSync` を直接使っており `hermeticEnv()` を通っていない。

同じ形（`spawnSync` を直接使い `hermeticEnv()` を通さない）のファイルは他に10:

```
aggregate_sub_issues / decide_turn_ending / extract_notify_tag / inject_uncommitted_notice /
parse_pr_metadata / read_run_ending / read_secret_names / redact_stream /
resolve_entry_agent / write_credentials_file
```

現に落ちるのは config を `machineryPath` 経由で読むファイルだけだが、同じ穴が開いている。

## 影響

CI は green のままなので**マージは止まらない**。影響を受けるのはエージェント自身で、`harness.ts` のコメントが記録している通り、これで1 run が丸ごと無駄になった例がある。このリポジトリの前提（「エージェントが実行するスイートは、自分の変更の結果としてだけ赤くなる」）が壊れている。

## 直し方（案）

`run_environment_setup.test.ts` の3つの `spawnSync` に `hermeticEnv()` を渡す（`runWithFakeGh` と同じ形）。他の10ファイルも同様に点検する。

Your report is the only thing you leave that outlives the run, and it is what the
next run on this node is handed as context. Write it for that reader first and for
a person second.

**The work itself is not one of the parts.** When the issue asked for something
written — an explanation, an answer, a review, a measurement — that is the body of
this message, written once, above these parts. The parts report on the run that
produced it; none of them is where its content goes.

What the machinery and GitHub already state is stated above. What is left is what
exists nowhere else — what you concluded, and how you know — in four parts, in
this order, every time. A part with nothing in it says so; none is dropped. Three
of the four have a ceiling, and a ceiling is a limit rather than a target.

**What you concluded.** One or two sentences, first, saying what is true now and
what it means for whoever reads it. Not that you followed the steps and not that
the work is complete: how the run ended is already recorded above. Two sentences
is the ceiling, not the opening move of a longer one.

**How you know.** Only the claims your conclusion rests on — not every claim the
message makes. Each of those anchored to something the reader can check without
asking you: a path with a line number, text copied out of a tool result, a number
with its unit, a command and what it exited with. Name the files. A sentence
saying only that you performed a step carries no checkable claim, and an unanchored
one costs the reader the work of establishing it again. Five items at most.

docs/work/how-it-works/the-branch-a-run-commits-to.md

# The branch a run commits to

- A branch is created at the first commit, not at the start of a run. A run that
  only reports, confirms a merge, or closes an issue leaves no branch behind.
- The name is `atomaton/issue-N`. A merge deletes the branch, so the same issue's
  next piece of work takes that name again, cut fresh from the base branch.
- If a merged branch is still there — a deletion that failed, or a merge made
  some other way — the next name counts up instead: `atomaton/issue-N-2`, then
  `atomaton/issue-N-3`. Work never resumes on merged history.
- When an unmerged branch is left behind, the issue's next run resumes it
  instead of starting from the base branch.
- A sub-issue's branch is cut from its parent's and merges back into it, so
  sibling tasks see each other's work as it lands. The parent's branch is created
  from the base branch when the first child commits — until then it does not
  exist — and reaches the base branch as one pull request once every child is
  done. Deployment is not dispatched for a merge into a parent branch: that work
  is still in progress, and only the final pull request into the base branch
  carries it to release.

Which branch the first of these is cut from is
[`base_branch`](../reference.md#base_branch), and the tree these branches follow is
[work is a tree of issues](work-is-a-tree-of-issues.md).

## 観測したこと

1. **PR #20 は `main` ではなく `atomaton/issue-16`（親ブランチ）にマージされた。** `github__get_pr(20)` → `"baseRefName":"atomaton/issue-16","state":"MERGED"`。子の work は親ブランチから切られ、親ブランチに戻る — `src/content/agent-definitions/atomaton.md:102` の「Each child merged into this issue's own branch rather than into the base」と、`src/adapters/github/branch-placement.ts:195-198` の `git checkout -b <name> origin/<親ブランチ>` がその実装。
2. **`main` には変更が無い。** `git show HEAD:src/content/prompt-template.md | grep -c -F 'Two sentences is the ceiling'` → **0**（`HEAD` = `44234b1`）。親ブランチ tip `30e3ab6` では同コマンドが **1**、`atomaton.md` の `The conclusion is written once.` も 0 → 1。
3. **`main` を名指す close 条件が満たせない。** #17 の本文「`main` 上で `src/content/prompt-template.md` が … を含み …」は、親ブランチが `main` に配送されるまで成立しない。
4. **その配送は #17 が閉じるまで起きない。** 親の再招集は `countOpenSiblings` が open な子を数える gate が握っており（`.github/atomaton-runtime/scripts/aggregate_sub_issues.ts:472`、`.github/atomaton-runtime/scripts/dispatch_if_siblings_done.ts:466-473`）、#17 は `state: OPEN` かつ `atomaton/launched` ラベル付き（`github__get_issue(17)`）で dispatch 通知もスレッドにある。#16 は `pull_requests: []` で、親ブランチの PR は存在しない。

**つまり：#17 は `main` を要求し、`main` は #16 の配送を要求し、#16 の配送は #17 のクローズを要求する。**

## この run が配送を試みた結果

`github__commit_and_push` を呼んだところ、ツールは子の work を親ブランチに載せようとして git に拒否された:

```
Could not create branch 'atomaton/issue-17': error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by checkout:
	src/content/agent-definitions/atomaton.md
	src/content/prompt-template.md
	src/entrypoints/tools/mcp/atomaton.ts
	tests/contract/agent-prompts.test.ts
Please commit your changes or stash them before you switch branches.
Aborting
```

これは `branch-placement.ts:195-198` が `origin/atomaton/issue-16` へ checkout しようとしたため。**仮に push が通っても PR の base は `atomaton/issue-16` になり**（`create_pr` の base 解決は「親ブランチがあればそれ」）、#17 の close 条件は満たせない。ブランチを `main` から切る手段はエージェントには無い（`git checkout`/`branch` は shell guard が拒否、`commit_and_push` のスキーマは `message` のみ）。

親ブランチ `30e3ab6` の親は `37f1c44`（v0.1.0）で、`main` から 47 ファイル差。このリポジトリの clone は shallow で `git merge-base` が答えないため、**親ブランチを `main` にマージしたときに何が一緒に入るかは検証していない。**

## 決めてほしいこと（コスト付き）

| 案 | 内容 | コスト |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A（推奨）** | 人が #16 に `/atomaton` を打ち、親ブランチの集約 PR を `main` へ出す（#18 の comment 5 に前例あり）。その後 #17 の再開 run が `main` を確認して閉じる | 人の操作1回＋親 run 1回。設計どおりの経路 |
| B | 人が #17 をこの証拠で手動クローズし、#16 の集約を進める | close 条件を `main` で確認せずに閉じる |
| C | #17 の close 条件を「マージされた PR の head / 親ブランチ」と読み替えて今閉じる | 子の close 条件の意味が変わる。**stacked な子すべてに効くので決定が要る** |
| D | 人が `atomaton/issue-16` → `main` の PR を直接開いてマージ | 47 ファイル差で、merge で何が入るか未検証（shallow clone のため） |

A を推す。閉じるべきなのは #17 の close 条件のほうではなく、配送の順序だから。

{"status":"completed","exit_code":0,"stdout":"/**
 * issue-links.ts — what an issue is attached to, and which attachments count.
 *
 * The relationships an issue has are the difference between reading a comment
 * correctly and reading it wrong. "Implemented it" on a sub-issue means a part
 * was implemented, not the feature. "We decided X" reads as settled when the
 * pull request carrying X is merged, and as a proposal when it is still open.
 * Neither is recoverable from the comment text.
 *
 * These are read from GitHub's own relationships rather than from Atomaton's
 * markers, because an issue a person drove by hand has no Atomaton markers on it
 * and is exactly the case that must not silently come back empty.
 *
 * Pure. The GraphQL half lives in `adapters/github/issue-links.ts`.
 */
import type { NodeState } from "./work-tree.ts";

export interface LinkedIssue {
  number: number;
  title: string;
  /**
   * How the work there stands, in the one vocabulary the tree uses.
   *
   * It was `string`, holding GitHub's own state lowercased, which is how this
   * module came to carry a second spelling of something `work-tree.ts` already
   * names — and why `LinkedPr` needed a `merged` flag beside it. See `NodeState`
   * for why `closed` was not an answer worth keeping.
   */
  state: NodeState;
}

/**
 * A sub-issue, with what a gate needs to judge it.
 *
 * `labels` is here and not on [`LinkedIssue`] because only the children are judged:
 * `sibling-check.ts` counts the ones Atomaton dispatched, and `work-tree.ts` needs to
 * know which are running before it stops a subtree. A parent or a pull request is
 * shown, not judged.
 *
 * It is also why the tool surface projects it away. These arrive in the same request
 * as the rest — one query, no extra round trip — but a label array per child in every
 * `get_issue` response is tokens spent on something no reader asked for.
 */
export interface LinkedChild extends LinkedIssue {
  readonly labels: readonly string[];
}

/**
 * A pull request linked to an issue.
 *
 * Nothing of its own any more. It carried `merged: boolean`, whose comment made
 * exactly the argument `NodeState` now makes — *GitHub says only `closed` for both
 * a merged pull request and an abandoned one, and those mean opposite things* —
 * and compensated for it with a second field. `state` answers it: a pull request
 * that is `done` is one that merged. Nothing ever read the flag.
 *
 * Kept as a name because the three lists on [`IssueLinks`] are three different
 * things and reading `LinkedIssue[]` for all of them would say they are not.
 */
export type LinkedPr = LinkedIssue;

{"content": "# #16 delivery run — notes for the next run on this node

## Where the work was

- `atomaton/issue-16` at `30e3ab6` = "Bound the report contract's parts and write the
  conclusion once (#20)". Its parent is `37f1c44` (InitialCommit, v0.1.0), which is
  **not an ancestor of `main`**. GitHub compare: `status: diverged, ahead_by: 1,
  behind_by: 61`, `merge_base_commit: 37f1c44`.
- So the old branch head had **none** of #17's change relative to `main`: the four
  files differed from `main` by 60 other files' worth of stale release (v0.15.0 vs
  v0.19.0) and by the change itself.
- Merging `30e3ab6` into `main` (base `37f1c44`) is not possible: `git merge-tree`
  reports conflicts on ~45 distinct paths, including all four intended files.

## What this run did

Rebuilt the branch's tree in place to **current `main` + the four #17 files**, then
committed it on top of `30e3ab6`. `commit_and_push` runs `git add -A` and commits to
the checked-out branch, so the commit's tree is what the worktree holds.

The worktree was made by `git archive origin/main | tar -x -C .` followed by
`patch -p1 < /tmp/atomaton-workspace/issue-17-on-main.patch`, and the index was then
rebuilt with `git read-tree origin/main` + `git update-index --add --cacheinfo` for
the four files. Both give tree `06e13adcd592343e94d5dad7e1a75f482295cdc6`.

Verified before committing:

- `git diff --cached --name-status origin/main` → exactly the four files.
- `git diff --cached --shortstat origin/main` → `4 files changed, 127 insertions(+), 9 deletions(-)`.
- `git diff --name-only` (index vs worktree) → empty.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=37f1c44 origin/main <tree>` → exit 0,
  zero conflicts, and the result tree is **byte-identical to** `06e13adc…` for every
  path. So merging this commit into `main` lands exactly `main` + the four changes,
  and nothing else.
- `bun run typecheck` exit 0; `bun run synth` exit 0;
  `bun run .github/atomaton-runtime/scripts/validate_deliverable.ts --root .` →
  `The deliverable in . is internally consistent.` exit 0.
- `bun run test` with the runner's `ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT` set → `1563 pass / 0 fail`,
  4433 expect() calls, exit 0.
- Negative control for the new contract test: `sed` each pinned fragment to `XXX`/`YYY`
  → `16 pass / 1 fail`; restored → `17 pass / 0 fail`.

## The one thing to know about the pull request

`create_pr` will show GitHub's **three-dot** diff (`merge-base 37f1c44 … head`), which
is ~156 files even though the merge changes four. If a reviewer reads the file list,
say plainly that the merge result is four files and that the display is the stale
merge base, not the change. `github__check_merge_readiness` may report
`governance-change` because the displayed list contains `.github/**`; the merge does

The four changes are PR #20's, unchanged; what is new is that they now sit on current `main` and are the only content difference.

## Why a new commit was needed

`atomaton/issue-16` was cut from `37f1c44` (`InitialCommit`, v0.1.0) and is **61 commits behind `main`**, at v0.15.0. GitHub's compare reports `status: diverged, ahead_by: 1, behind_by: 61, merge_base_commit: 37f1c44`. PR #20 merged #17's work into that stale branch, so `main` has none of the change — and the old head cannot simply be merged:

```
git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=37f1c44 origin/main 30e3ab6
→ exit 1, 134 conflict-stage entries over 46 distinct paths
   (src/content/prompt-template.md, src/content/agent-definitions/atomaton.md,
    src/entrypoints/tools/mcp/atomaton.ts, tests/contract/agent-prompts.test.ts
    are all among them)
```

So this commit sets the branch's tree to `main` plus those four files and nothing else, on top of `30e3ab6` so the history is kept.

## Read the merge, not the file list

GitHub shows the **three-dot** diff against the stale merge base, so the page will list ~156 files even though the merge changes four. The measurement that matters:

```
git diff --stat origin/main 282f8df
 src/content/agent-definitions/atomaton.md |  7 +++
 src/content/prompt-template.md            | 25 +++++---
 src/entrypoints/tools/mcp/atomaton.ts     |  8 ++-
 tests/contract/agent-prompts.test.ts      | 96 ++++++++++++++++++++++++
 4 files changed, 127 insertions(+), 9 deletions(-)

git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=37f1c44 origin/main 282f8df
→ exit 0, zero conflicts; result tree 06e13adcd592… is byte-identical to this
  commit's tree for every path
```

The second command is the whole claim: merging this lands `main` plus those four files, and nothing else. Nothing `main` has is removed — including #87's paragraph in `atomaton.md` and the `pretest` hooks in `package.json`, which copying stale files wholesale would have taken out.

`github__check_merge_readiness` may report `governance-change` because the displayed list contains `.github/**`. The merge does not touch `.github/**` or `self/**`; `git diff --name-status origin/main HEAD` lists four files, none of them governed.

## Verification, each run in this session on this tree

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `bun run typecheck` | exit 0 |
| `bun run synth` | exit 0, wrote `.github/atomaton-release.json` for v0.19.0 (91 files) |
| `bun run .github/atomaton-runtime/scripts/validate_deliverable.ts --root . --report /tmp/q.txt` | `The deliverable in . is internally consistent.`, exit 0 |
| `bun run test` with the runner's `ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT=/home/runner/work/_temp/atomaton-machinery` | `1563 pass / 0 fail`, 4433 expect() calls, `Ran 1563 tests across 129 files`, exit 0 |
| Negative control — `sed` the pinned fragments to `XXX`/`YYY` | `16 pass / 1 fail` (the new contract test) |
| Restored | `17 pass / 0 fail` |
| `git diff --name-only` (index vs worktree) before committing | empty |

The issue's close condition asks for four fragments. Measured with `grep -c -F` on this tree: `Two sentences is the ceiling` 1, `Five items at most.` 1, `with no ceiling, because it is the one that goes missing.` 1 in `src/content/prompt-template.md`; `The conclusion is written once.` 1 in `src/content/agent-definitions/atomaton.md`.

The change itself is described in PR #20 and unchanged from it, including the two deliberate points it recorded: the second heading stays `How you know` (the spelling `tests/contract/agent-prompts.test.ts` pins, against the specification block's `How I know`), and `Two sentences is the ceiling` sits on its own line so it is findable as a substring. PR #20's extra `config.yaml` hunk is **not** here — `main` already has `agents.on_config_finding` at line 139 of both copies.

---

### What I concluded

The four-file change now reaches `main` as a single clean merge, and the branch that carried it no longer has to be rescued by hand: `git merge-tree` against `main` exits 0 and its result is exactly `main` plus the four files, so the pull request's merge is the delivery. The three-dot file count on this page is the stale merge base, not the change.

### How I know

- `git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=37f1c44 origin/main 282f8df` → exit 0, zero conflicts, first line `06e13adcd592343e94d5dad7e1a75f482295cdc6`; `git ls-tree -r` of that tree and of `282f8df^{tree}` compare equal as sorted listings.
- `git diff --stat origin/main HEAD` → `4 files changed, 127 insertions(+), 9 deletions(-)`, the four paths named above; `git diff --diff-filter=A --name-only origin/main HEAD` → 0.
- `bun run test` with `ATOMATON_MACHINERY_ROOT` set → `1563 pass / 0 fail`, `4433 expect() calls`, exit 0; `bun run typecheck` exit 0; `validate_deliverable.ts --root .` → `The deliverable in . is internally consistent.` exit 0.
- The close condition's four fragments each `grep -c -F` → 1 at the paths above; the negative control (each pinned fragment replaced by `XXX`/`YYY`) → `16 pass / 1 fail` on `tests/contract/agent-prompts.test.ts`, restored → `17 pass / 0 fail`, so the test is what holds them.
- `.github/atomaton/config.yaml:139` and `self/atomaton/config.yaml:139` both read `on_config_finding: engineer` on `main`, which is why PR #20's config hunk is not carried here.

### What I could not establish

- **The old head's 60 other files were dropped on my judgement, not the issue's instruction.** `main` holds v0.19.0 and the branch held v0.15.0, so keeping them would have undone v0.16.0–v0.19.0. I did not enumerate what those four releases changed; I relied on `main` being the newer release and on the merge result being byte-identical to `main` + the four files.
- **`git merge-base` answers nothing in this clone** — `.git/shallow` truncates history at `37f1c44`/`main`, so every three-way computation here passes `--merge-base=37f1c44` explicitly, taking that SHA from GitHub's compare response. If GitHub's real merge base for this pull request differs, the simulation is one input wrong.
- **Whether GitHub will compute the same clean merge.** `git merge-tree` on git 2.55 with an explicitly supplied base is a local model of it; I could not make GitHub perform the merge, and `mergeable` is only reported after the pull request exists.
- **The reviewer will see ~156 files.** I could not find a way to make the display show four; a reviewer trusting the page rather than the merge has to read this body's measurement to avoid concluding that v0.15.0 is being restored.
- The three `run_environment_setup` failures #18 recorded are fixed on `main` (`hermeticEnv` count 4 in that test file) and are not re-measured here beyond the green suite above, so I did not independently re-derive that #18's cause is gone — only that the suite it made red is green in the agent's own environment.

### What happens next

`reviewer` reviews this pull request once CI passes; `pull-request-checks (verify)` runs `synth` before `test`, which is the sequence this tree was measured with. If a person merges it, the merge changes exactly the four files on `main`, and the re-invoked run on #16 reads that tree against the close condition and concludes the issue. Notes and a recovery copy of the pre-rebuild branch tree (`30e3ab6`) are in `/tmp/atomaton-workspace/issue-16-notes.md` and `/tmp/recover-30e3ab6/`."}
